```{python}
#| include: false
import sys
from coolpath import ROOT
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "notebooks"))
from _site import table, md, fig, chart, pct, num, C
from coolpath import load_config
from coolpath.transit import station_display
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
s6, s7, s8 = table("phase_06_summary.json"), table("phase_07_stats.json"), table("phase_08_scenarios.json")
s10, s10r, s10f, s10s = (table(n) for n in ("phase_10_city.json", "phase_10_city_routes.json", "phase_10_city_frontier.json",
                                            "phase_10_sensitivity.json"))
p6 = pd.DataFrame(s6["at_15h"]).query("sample == 'city'").set_index(["mode", "length_bin"])
p7 = pd.DataFrame(s7["by_mode_bin_15h"]).set_index(["mode", "length_bin"])
cfg = load_config()
r = p6.loc[("rapid", "300-800")]
b = p6.loc[("bus", "300-800")]
DAYS = {f"{d[5:7]}{d[8:10]}": pd.Timestamp(d).strftime("%B %-d") for d in cfg["study"]["dates"]}
D0 = list(DAYS)[0]
KEY = [f"{k}_{cfg['study']['key_hour']:02d}" for k in DAYS]
```

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(f"All numbers are for 15:00 ({' and '.join(DAYS.values())}, 2025, pooled) with the dynamic θ, unless stated. "
      "Each hour is the hour ending then, with the sun of half an hour earlier (15:00 = the sun at 14:30), for sun and heat alike. "
      "The **shadiest** walk minimises the shade cost, the **coolest** walk the heat (UTCI) cost; see [Methods](methods.qmd).")
```

## How much sun can a walk home avoid?

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(f"""<div class="label">Walks of 300–800 m from rapid-transit stations, 15:00 (the Story shows frequent bus stops; both are in the table)</div>

::: {{.stat-row}}
<div><div class="v sun">{pct(r.short_sun_share, 0)}</div><div class="label">of the shortest walk is sunny</div></div>
<div><div class="v">−{pct(r.sun_red_mean, 0)}</div><div class="label">sun on the shadiest walk</div></div>
<div><div class="v">+{pct(r.detour_mean, 2)}</div><div class="label">extra distance</div></div>
<div><div class="v">{pct(p7.loc[('rapid', '300-800')].no_alt_share, 0)}</div><div class="label">of walks have no cooler option</div></div>
:::""")
```

```{python}
#| column: page-inset-right
t = pd.DataFrame({
    "Mode": [("Rapid" if m == "rapid" else "Bus") for m, _ in p6.index],
    "Walk": [l.replace("-", "–") + "\u00a0m" for _, l in p6.index],
    "Walks": p6.trips.astype(int).map("{:,}".format).values,
    "Sun on shortest": [pct(x, 0) for x in p6.short_sun_share],
    "Sun ↓": [pct(x, 1) for x in p6.sun_red_mean],
    "Detour (mean / 95th pct.)": [f"{pct(a, 1)} / {pct(b, 1)}" for a, b in zip(p6.detour_mean, p6.detour_p95)],
    "Exposure ↓": [pct(x, 2) for x in p6.exposure_red_mean],
    "No cooler option": [pct(p7.loc[i].no_alt_share, 0) for i in p6.index],
})
md(t)
```

Rapid = rapid-transit stations; Bus = frequent bus stops. Sun ↓ = sun reduction of the shadiest walk; Exposure ↓ = weighted exposure reduction.

```{python}
#| output: asis
lo, hi = p6.detour_p95.min(), p6.detour_p95.max()
print(f"- **The shadiest walk is rarely more than a few percent longer.** Mean detours stay below 1% in every group, and 95% of "
      f"shadiest walks are at most {pct(lo, 1)}–{pct(hi, 1)} longer than the shortest walk, depending on the group.")
```

- **Rapid-transit walks gain more** than bus walks of the same length: stations sit in denser, taller parts of the city where a parallel street in building shade is usually available.
- **Short walks have no choice.** Under 300 m, more than four in five walks have no cooler option.
- **Weighted exposure falls much less than sun.** With θ near 0.2, a metre moved from sun into shade lowers the cost by only 0.2 m; the remaining heat burden of shaded walking is still counted.

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "Sun reduction by hour, walks of 300–800 m (dynamic θ)."
bt = table("phase_06_by_time.csv")
bt = bt[(bt["sample"] == "city") & (bt.length_bin == "300-800")]
f, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 3.4))
for (mode, day), g in bt.assign(day=bt.time.str[:4]).groupby(["mode", "day"]):
    g = g.sort_values("time")
    ax.plot(g.time.str[5:].astype(int), 100 * g.sun_red_mean, marker="o", ms=3,
            color=C["sun"] if mode == "rapid" else C["cool"], ls="-" if day == D0 else "--",
            label=f"{'rapid transit' if mode == 'rapid' else 'bus'}, {DAYS[day]}")
ax.set(xlabel="hour", ylabel="sun reduction (%)", xticks=range(8, 20))
ax.legend(fontsize=9, ncol=2)
chart(f)
```

Morning and evening, when shadows are long, offer the most; around 13:00–14:00 the sun is high and little shade is left to choose.

## From sun to heat

```{python}
#| output: asis
bh = pd.DataFrame(s10["by_hour"]).set_index("label")
k0 = KEY[0]
h0 = bh.loc[k0]
print(f"""Shade is yes or no; heat is a temperature. The SOLWEIG model gives the UTCI, the temperature the weather feels like to
the body, at every sidewalk point for the same 24 hours. On {DAYS[D0]} at 15:00 a typical sunlit sidewalk felt like
{h0.u_sun:.1f} °C, at the edge of *extreme* heat stress (46 °C); one step into shade took off about
{h0.u_sun - (h0.u_bldg + h0.u_tree) / 2:.0f} °C.

<div class="label">Median UTCI of sidewalk points, {DAYS[D0]}, 15:00</div>

::: {{.stat-row}}
<div><div class="v sun">{h0.u_sun:.1f} °C</div><div class="label">in the sun</div></div>
<div><div class="v">{h0.u_bldg:.1f} °C</div><div class="label">in building shade</div></div>
<div><div class="v">{h0.u_tree:.1f} °C</div><div class="label">in tree shade</div></div>
<div><div class="v">{num(h0.u_tree - h0.u_sun, '.1f')} °C</div><div class="label">tree shade against sun</div></div>
:::""")
```

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "Median UTCI of sidewalk points in the sun, in tree shade and in building shade, by hour (shade classes from our shadow model). Bands: UTCI heat-stress categories."
f, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 3.8))
for lo_b, hi_b, name in ((32, 38, "strong"), (38, 46, "very strong"), (46, 50, "extreme")):
    ax.axhspan(lo_b, hi_b, color=C["sun"], alpha={"strong": 0.04, "very strong": 0.08, "extreme": 0.16}[name], lw=0)
    ax.text(19.6, (lo_b + min(hi_b, 48)) / 2, name, ha="left", va="center", fontsize=8, color=C["dim"], clip_on=False)
for day, ls in zip(DAYS, ("-", "--")):
    g = bh[bh.index.str.startswith(day)]
    hrs = g.index.str[5:].astype(int)
    for col, colr, nm in (("u_sun", C["sun"], "sun"), ("u_tree", C["tree"], "tree shade"), ("u_bldg", C["bldg"], "building shade")):
        ax.plot(hrs, g[col], color=colr, ls=ls, lw=2, label=f"{nm}, {DAYS[day]}")
ax.set(xlabel="hour", ylabel="UTCI (°C)", xticks=range(8, 20), ylim=(30, 48), xlim=(7.8, 19.5))
ax.legend(fontsize=8, ncol=2, loc="lower center")
chart(f)
```

```{python}
#| output: asis
tr = bh.loc[KEY].tree_relief
mo = bh[bh.index.str.endswith("_08")].tree_relief.mean()
g0b = bh[bh.index.str.startswith(D0)]
vs = g0b[g0b.u_bldg > 38].index.str[5:].astype(int)
print(f"""- **Tree shade is as cool as building shade.** The shade cost of Wen et al. counts a metre of tree shade as half as good
  as building shade. In the heat model, tree shade at 15:00 takes off {pct(tr.min(), 0)}–{pct(tr.max(), 0)} of the step from
  sun to building shade, slightly more than building shade itself ({pct(mo, 0)} at 8:00): in the afternoon, walls and pavement
  that stood in the sun all day still radiate heat into shaded streets, while a tree also shades the ground under it.
- **Shade does not make a walk comfortable.** Even building shade stays at *very strong* heat stress (above 38 °C) from
  {vs.min()}:00 to {vs.max()}:00 on {DAYS[D0]}. Choosing the shaded side lowers the strain; it does not remove it.""")
```

### The coolest walk home

```{python}
#| output: asis
mb = pd.DataFrame(s10r["by_mode_bin_key_hour"]).set_index(["mode", "length_bin"])
nd = len(s10r["dates"])
hb = mb.loc[("bus", "300-800")]
print(f"""Routing on the UTCI instead of the shade classes gives the **coolest walk**. For walks of 300–800 m from frequent bus stops
at 15:00:

::: {{.stat-row}}
<div><div class="v">{num(hb.heat_dutci, '.2f')} °C</div><div class="label">mean UTCI on the coolest walk (shadiest {num(hb.shade_dutci, '.2f')})</div></div>
<div><div class="v">+{pct(hb.heat_detour, 2)}</div><div class="label">extra distance (shadiest +{pct(hb.shade_detour, 2)})</div></div>
<div><div class="v">−{pct(hb.heat_extreme_red, 0)}</div><div class="label">metres of extreme heat (shadiest −{pct(hb.shade_extreme_red, 0)})</div></div>
<div><div class="v">{pct(hb.heat_eq_shade, 0)}</div><div class="label">same path as the shadiest walk</div></div>
:::""")
```

```{python}
#| column: page-inset-right
md(pd.DataFrame({
    "Mode": [("Rapid" if m == "rapid" else "Bus") for m, _ in mb.index],
    "Walk": [l.replace("-", "\u2060–\u2060") + "\u00a0m" for _, l in mb.index],
    "UTCI, shortest": [f"{x:.1f} °C" for x in mb.short_utci],
    "Extreme heat, shortest": [f"{x:.0f} m" for x in mb.short_extreme_m],
    "Shadiest: UTCI / detour": [f"{num(a, '.2f')} °C / +{pct(b, 2)}" for a, b in zip(mb.shade_dutci, mb.shade_detour)],
    "Coolest: UTCI / detour": [f"{num(a, '.2f')} °C / +{pct(b, 2)}" for a, b in zip(mb.heat_dutci, mb.heat_detour)],
    "Extreme heat ↓ shadiest / coolest": [f"{pct(a, 0)} / {pct(b, 0)}" for a, b in zip(mb.shade_extreme_red, mb.heat_extreme_red)],
    "Coolest = shadiest": [pct(x, 0) for x in mb.heat_eq_shade],
}))
```

Walk counts as in the sun table above. UTCI = mean UTCI along the walk, change against the shortest walk. Extreme heat = metres with UTCI ≥ 46 °C on the shortest walk, and the mean reduction for walks that have any.

```{python}
#| output: asis
bt = pd.DataFrame(s10r["by_time"]).set_index("time")
g0 = bt[bt.index.str.startswith(D0)]
hr = g0.index.str[5:].astype(int)
best = g0.heat_dutci.idxmin()
noon = g0[(hr >= 11) & (hr <= 15)].heat_dutci.idxmax()
eve = g0.index[-1]
rp = mb.loc[("rapid", "300-800")]
mid = mb.xs("300-800", level="length_bin").heat_eq_shade
xr = mb.heat_extreme_red / mb.shade_extreme_red
print(f"""- **The two walks mostly agree.** For {pct(mid.min(), 0)}–{pct(mid.max(), 0)} of walks of 300–800 m the coolest walk is the
  shadiest walk. Where they differ, the coolest walk takes the tree-lined street the shade cost undervalues, and tells apart
  sunny streets that are hotter or cooler than usual.
- **The coolest walk is a little cooler, for a little more distance.** It lowers the walk's mean UTCI by about
  {num(-(mb.heat_dutci - mb.shade_dutci).mean(), '.1f')} °C more than the shadiest walk and cuts the metres of extreme heat
  stress {xr.min():.1f}–{xr.max():.1f} times as much, for mean detours of {pct(mb.heat_detour.min(), 1)}–{pct(mb.heat_detour.max(), 1)}.
- **Rapid-transit walks gain most**, as with sun: {num(rp.heat_dutci, '.2f')} °C for walks of 300–800 m, against
  {num(hb.heat_dutci, '.2f')} °C from bus stops.
- **Averages are small because most walks have no choice.** The mean over all walks, sunny or not, hides walks with no
  alternative (a change of 0) next to walks that cool by several degrees. Like shade, the gain is largest in the morning
  ({num(g0.loc[best, 'heat_dutci'], '.2f')} °C at {best[5:]}:00 on {DAYS[D0]}, all walks) and small around midday
  ({num(g0.loc[noon, 'heat_dutci'], '.2f')} °C at {noon[5:]}:00), when little shade is left. Unlike shade, it is small again
  in the evening ({num(g0.loc[eve, 'heat_dutci'], '.2f')} °C at {eve[5:]}:00): the shadows are long, but the low sun no longer
  makes the sunny side much hotter.""")
```

### Why the coolest walk is cooler

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "Same detour, cooler walk: mean detour and mean UTCI reduction of walks of at least 300 m at 15:00 (both days), for three costs with θ fixed from 0.05 to 0.6."
fr = pd.DataFrame(s10f["rows"])
names = {"shade": ("shade cost, tree = ½ building (Wen et al.)", C["bldg"]),
         "shade_tf1": ("shade cost, tree = building", C["tree"]), "heat": ("UTCI cost", C["sun"])}
f, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.5, 3.8))
for k, (nm, colr) in names.items():
    g = fr[fr.cost == k].sort_values("theta")
    ax.plot(100 * g.detour, -g.dutci, color=colr, lw=2, marker="o", ms=4, label=nm)
ax.set(xlabel="mean detour (%)", ylabel="UTCI reduction (°C)", xlim=(0, 100 * fr.detour.max() * 1.05), ylim=(0, None))
ax.legend(fontsize=9, loc="lower right")
chart(f)
```

```{python}
#| output: asis
import numpy as np
sh_ = fr[fr.cost == "shade"].sort_values("detour")
t1_ = fr[(fr.cost == "shade_tf1") & (fr.detour <= fr[fr.cost == "shade"].detour.max())].sort_values("detour")
hh_ = fr[(fr.cost == "heat") & (fr.detour <= sh_.detour.max())]
gain = hh_.dutci / np.interp(hh_.detour, sh_.detour, sh_.dutci) - 1
gt = t1_.dutci / np.interp(t1_.detour, sh_.detour, sh_.dutci) - 1
print(f"""Is the coolest walk cooler only because it is allowed to detour more? Fixing θ at a range of values traces, for each cost,
how much cooler walks get for a given extra distance. At the same detour the UTCI cost cools walks
{pct(gain.min(), 0)}–{pct(gain.max(), 0)} more than the shade cost. Valuing tree shade as much as building shade adds only
about {pct(gt.mean(), 0)}: most of the gain comes from the differences *within* each shade class, such as a sunny metre next to
hot walls against one on an open lawn, or a deep street canyon against a thin strip of shade.""")
```

```{python}
#| output: asis
ts = pd.DataFrame(s10s["transmissivity_by_hour"]).set_index(["hour", "transmissivity"]).tree_relief
kh = cfg["study"]["key_hour"]
mg = pd.DataFrame(s10s["margin800"]["by_hour"])
print(f"""**How robust is this?** SOLWEIG lets a fixed 3% of the sun through tree crowns. Rerunning {s10s['tau05']['cores']} tiles of
{DAYS[D0]} with 5% and 15% moves tree shade's share of the building-shade relief at {kh}:00 from {pct(ts.loc[(kh, 0.03)], 0)}
to {pct(ts.loc[(kh, 0.05)], 0)} and {pct(ts.loc[(kh, 0.15)], 0)}: thinner crowns make tree shade warmer, but it stays about as
cool as building shade, far from the half assumed by the shade cost. Widening the margin around each tile from 400 to 800 m,
so that towers further away can cast shadows in, changes the UTCI by more than 0.5 °C at no more than
{pct(mg['share_abs_gt_0.5'].max(), 2)} of points in any hour. Details: [technical notes](technical.qmd).""")
```

## Through buildings (University City)

```{python}
#| column: page-inset-right
d = pd.DataFrame(s8["at_15h"])
d = d[d.set != "home"]
lab = {"outdoor": "Outdoor only", "no_penncard": "+ buildings open without a Penn ID", "all": "+ all mapped buildings"}
order = ["outdoor", "no_penncard", "all"]
d["o"] = d.scenario.map(order.index)
d = d.sort_values(["set", "o"])
md(pd.DataFrame({"Sample": d.set.map({"campus": "Campus", "station": "Station"}),
                 "Scenario": d.scenario.map(lab), "Walks": d.trips.astype(int).map("{:,}".format).values,
                 "Shadiest uses indoors": [pct(x, 0) for x in d.shade_uses_indoor],
                 "Sun ↓*": [pct(x, 1) for x in d.sun_red_vs_outdoor],
                 "Exposure ↓*": [pct(x, 1) for x in d.exposure_red_vs_outdoor],
                 "Length*": [f"+{100 * x:.2f}%" for x in d.len_vs_outdoor]}))
```

Campus = building to building; Station = rapid-transit station to building. \* compared with the shortest walk on the outdoor-only network. Indoor passages have no UTCI, so this section uses the shade cost only.

```{python}
#| output: asis
u = d.set_index(["set", "scenario"])
bb = pd.DataFrame(s8["at_15h_by_bin"]).query("scenario == 'all' and set != 'home'").set_index(["set", "length_bin"]).shade_uses_indoor
lo_, hi_ = sorted(bb.loc[(k, "800-1200")] / bb.loc[(k, "300-800")] for k in ("campus", "station"))
print(f"Opening the annotated buildings puts about one in five shadiest walks indoors and removes another "
      f"{100 * (u.loc[('campus', 'all')].sun_red_vs_outdoor - u.loc[('campus', 'outdoor')].sun_red_vs_outdoor):.1f}–"
      f"{100 * (u.loc[('station', 'all')].sun_red_vs_outdoor - u.loc[('station', 'outdoor')].sun_red_vs_outdoor):.1f} points of sun, "
      "without making walks longer. The Indoor Contribution Index stays close to zero (median below 0.001 in absolute value): "
      "indoor passages here offer an equally long but cooler option, not a shortcut. This differs from the Dubai stations of Wen et al. "
      "(2025), where indoor networks through malls and connected towers make indoor routes real shortcuts. With θ near 0.2–0.3 for most of a "
      "300–1,200 m walk, an indoor metre beats building shade by only about 0.1 m of cost, so indoor routes are chosen mainly when they "
      f"are already on the way; walks of 800–1,200 m use them {lo_:.1f}–{hi_:.1f} times as often as walks of 300–800 m.")
```

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "University City at 15:00: share of the sun avoided compared with the shortest outdoor walk, and share of shadiest walks that go indoors."
lab2 = {"outdoor": "Outdoor only", "no_penncard": "+ buildings open without a Penn ID", "all": "+ all mapped buildings"}
cols = {"outdoor": C["dim"], "no_penncard": "#8f78c9", "all": C["indoor"]}
f, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(7.2, 2.9), sharey=True)

for k, (ax, (col, title)) in enumerate(zip(axes, [("sun_red_vs_outdoor", "sun avoided"), ("shade_uses_indoor", "shadiest walk goes indoors")])):
    for i, (sname, slab) in enumerate(sets):
        for j, sc in enumerate(order):
            v = u.loc[(sname, sc)][col]
            y = i * 1.25 + j * 0.36
            ax.barh(y, 100 * v, height=0.3, color=cols[sc], label=lab2[sc] if i == 0 and k == 0 else None)
            ax.text(100 * v + 0.6, y, f"{100 * v:.0f}%", va="center", fontsize=9, color=C["ink"])
    ax.set_title(title, fontsize=10, color=C["ink"], loc="left")
    ax.set_xlim(0, 25); ax.xaxis.set_visible(False); ax.grid(False)
    for sp in ("left", "bottom"):
        ax.spines[sp].set_visible(False)
axes[0].set_yticks([0.36, 1.25 + 0.36], [s for _, s in sets]); axes[0].tick_params(axis="y", length=0)

chart(f)
```

## Limitations

- Outside University City, campus and park walkways are missing, so cooler options there are understated.
- “No cooler option” mixes two cases: no cooler street exists, or one exists but is not worth the detour at the default shade preference.
- Shadows and heat are for two hot, sunny days, June 24 and July 29, 2025; trees from leaf-off LiDAR and 2018 land cover; buildings from 2022.
- Air temperature, humidity and wind come from one ERA5 weather cell and are the same on every street; the heat map shows the
  effect of sun, shade and surfaces, not neighbourhood differences in air temperature or the cooling of a breezy street.
- Trees let a fixed 3% of the sun through in SOLWEIG; leafier or sparser crowns would change how much cooler tree shade is
  (see the sensitivity test above).
- UTCI is for a standing person in the open air; air-conditioned indoor passages have no UTCI, so the coolest walk stays outdoors.
- Indoor passages assume buildings are open and air-conditioned; opening hours and security are not modelled.
